```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

tsorder selects the order of a time-series model. It puts three families of
estimators side by side, all computed by one dependency-free Rust core:

* **information criteria** (AIC, AICc, BIC, HQ, FPE, CAT, MDL) over nested
  fits by Yule-Walker, Burg or conditional least squares;
* **threshold ("clip") estimators** in the tradition of Fine and Hwang
  (1979): grow the memory with the sample, studentise a statistic (PACF,
  Bartlett-studentised ACF, inverse PACF, the Jirak band, a robust PACF),
  and keep the last lag that noise cannot explain;
* **McMillan-degree estimators** (the state dimension): Bauer's SVC on
  past-future canonical correlations, a calibrated Hankel singular-value
  cut, and a sequential rank test.

Every default was chosen by a reproducible benchmark shipped in the
repository, and the test suite pins the implementation to R itself
(`stats::ar.yw`, `robustbase::Qn`, `TSA::eacf`) and to published tables
(Bauer 2001, Table 1).

## One call

```{r}
library(tsorder)
set.seed(1)
x <- arima.sim(list(ar = c(1.2, -0.6)), 400)

fit <- order_select(x)   # PACF-clip with the benchmark-chosen defaults
fit
```

The whole decision path comes along, ready to plot:

```{r}
ggplot2::autoplot(fit)
```

Criteria work the same way:

```{r}
order_select(x, method = "bic")$order
ic_order(x, criterion = "bic", method = "burg")$order
```

## MA and ARMA orders

```{r}
y <- arima.sim(list(ma = c(0.6, 0.3)), 2000)
fh_order(y, statistic = "acf_bartlett")$order   # MA order via Bartlett band
fh_order(y, statistic = "inverse_pacf")$order   # MA order via the inverse PACF

z <- arima.sim(list(ar = 0.5, ma = 0.5), 1000)
hannan_rissanen(z)[c("p", "q")]                 # ARMA (p, q)
```

## When there is measurement noise, change the target

Observation noise turns an AR(p) into an ARMA(p, p) but leaves the state
dimension unchanged, so the McMillan-degree route keeps working while
AR-order selectors drift:

```{r}
noisy <- x + rnorm(length(x), sd = 1)
c(ar_order_bic = ic_order(noisy, "bic")$order,
  mcmillan = svc_order(noisy)$order)
```

## From selection to a fitted model

`fit_arima()` closes the loop: it estimates the order of integration,
selects the order on the differenced series, and returns a standard
`stats::arima()` fit -- which means the rest of the ecosystem just works,
including `forecast`:

```{r}
fit <- fit_arima(x)           # ARIMA(2, 0, 0) here
fit
predict(fit, n.ahead = 4)$pred
```

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("forecast", quietly = TRUE)}
forecast::forecast(fit, h = 6)
```

`order_select()` results also follow the broom conventions, for tidy
pipelines:

```{r}
f <- order_select(x)
generics::glance(f)
head(generics::tidy(f))
```

## How many differences

```{r}
rw <- cumsum(as.numeric(x))
integration_order(rw)$d
```

The level of the sequential test vanishes with the sample size, so `d` is
estimated consistently; difference `d` times and proceed with the
stationary tools above.
